主要内容: The Federal Reserve issued Supervisory Letter SR 12-17 / CA 12-14 on December 17, 2012, outlining a consolidated supervision framework for large financial institutions. This framework was revised on October 1, 2025, to remove references to reputational risk. The letter emphasizes enhancing the resiliency of financial institutions to withstand internal and external stresses, ensuring they maintain sufficient capital, liquidity, and operational resilience. It also aims to reduce the impact on the financial system and broader economy in the event of a firm’s failure or material weakness. The framework incorporates both microprudential and macroprudential considerations, aligning with provisions of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act. The guidance does not apply to community banking organizations, defined as institutions with total consolidated assets of $10 billion or less. The framework outlines a tailored supervisory approach for large financial institutions, focusing on systemic risk and firm-specific vulnerabilities. It applies to LISCC firms, which are the largest and most complex U.S. and foreign financial organizations subject to consolidated supervision. Nonbank financial companies designated by the FSOC are also included. Large Banking Organizations (LBOs) and Large Foreign Banking Organizations (Large FBOs) are defined based on their consolidated assets. The framework emphasizes enhancing resiliency through capital and liquidity planning, corporate governance, recovery planning, and resolution strategies. The Federal Reserve may identify additional priorities beyond these core areas to improve supervision and address risks to financial stability. Effective supervision requires cooperation with other regulators and a comprehensive understanding of each firm's condition.
